mbm-1251.clue: My gym towel was crowned champion.
mbm-1251.quote: My friend folded the corners of my towel into points after I finished my first full lifting program. I draped it on the empty bar and we bowed to the new champion. It had done most of the mopping up.

mbm-1252.quote: I threaded a bracelet to match my grandmother’s garden after rain. The clear bead is the puddle by the gate. Hold it to the light and you can see all the other colors swimming inside.

mbm-1253.clue: I turned the handle into a tail.
mbm-1253.quote: My clay teacup came out wonderfully lopsided. I gave it two pointed ears and curled the handle like a cat’s tail. It sits quietly until my brother starts pouring the milk.

mbm-1254.clue: I keep sand in a glass bottle.
mbm-1254.quote: I filled a little vial after my friends and I played beach volleyball on the coldest day of spring. In the photograph we’re wearing sweatshirts and laughing under the net. The sand looks deceptively warm.

mbm-1255.clue: I recognized the tree by its elbow.
mbm-1255.quote: My canoe drifted around a bend where a crooked branch reaches down like a bent arm. I’d drawn that branch from shore the winter before. It felt like meeting an old friend from the other side.

mbm-1256.quote: I made a patchwork picture of our little cinema after it closed. The seats are red velvet and the screen is a blank white square. My mum says she can fill that square with whatever film she likes.

mbm-1257.quote: Under canopy I saw a red barn, a flash of yellow sunlight, a blue bend of river and green grass around the landing circle. I drew the four colors in my jump log before I even took off my boots.

mbm-1258.clue: I take a biscuit tin to book club.
mbm-1258.quote: We tuck questions about the novel into the tin and draw them after tea. Last time I pulled my own question and changed my mind about the answer while I was reading it aloud.

mbm-1259.clue: Our dragon has a velvet cold.
mbm-1259.quote: I stitched a red handkerchief to my glove puppet’s paw when the dragon got a sniffle in our winter story. The children keep asking after him. He now sneezes politely before every entrance.

mbm-1260.clue: I taught my computer to keep a secret.
mbm-1260.quote: My sister asked for a diary program with a dragon at the gate. I drew the dragon knitting during the password prompt. She named it Agnes and types slowly so it can finish its row.

mbm-1261.clue: I run one block for the music.
mbm-1261.quote: Somebody practices piano beside the steepest part of my route. On a hard morning I promise myself one more block to hear the tune. I’ve made it through three movements of a sonata that way.

mbm-1262.clue: My ski gloves have an extra purpose.
mbm-1262.quote: My mum wears one like a puppet from the boat when I’m getting tired on the water skis. It nods so gravely I have to grin. I made the new pair with one red thumb for its nose.

mbm-1263.clue: I made a quilt you can wear as wings.
mbm-1263.quote: My niece asked for a butterfly blanket. I added two soft loops near the corners so she can stand up from a nap and flutter straight into breakfast.

mbm-1264.quote: We use a big cork from my uncle’s bottle as the mountain on our homemade board. The path spirals around it in green pen. He still lifts the cork after every game to see whether the climbers came home.

mbm-1265.clue: I draw the wind rather than the hole.
mbm-1265.quote: I started marking arrows in my golf notebook when my drives drifted. Now the page looks like a flock of tiny birds crossing every fairway. On a still day I leave the page gloriously blank.

mbm-1266.clue: I once had to play around dessert.
mbm-1266.quote: A chestnut fell right into my putting line. My playing partner cooked it with supper and brought me the shell next week. It lives in my ball pocket as a reminder that trees get a turn too.

mbm-1267.clue: I redraw the same second of film.
mbm-1267.quote: Our anime club pauses at the instant a character decides whether to smile. We sketch just the mouths. I’ve never seen so many different answers to one tiny question.

mbm-1268.clue: I bought a candle for my bowling ball.
mbm-1268.quote: For my bowling league’s birthday night we stuck a candle in a cupcake shaped like a purple ball. I blew it out and rolled a spare. The cupcake had better aim at my shirt than my ball had at the pins.

mbm-1269.clue: I always put the lantern card on top.
mbm-1269.quote: I beat my big brother once with a card showing a tiny lantern keeper. He drew a paper lantern to hang over our next match. Even when the keeper loses, it feels like playing at home.

mbm-1270.clue: My chalk bag has a little skylight.
mbm-1270.quote: I patched a hole in the bag with bright blue cloth. On a gray climbing day I reach for chalk and find one square of sky. My partner keeps asking whether the forecast in there has changed.

mbm-1271.clue: I stick the flag in my shoe.
mbm-1271.quote: When we play beach volleyball on a windy afternoon our paper score flag blows away. I plant it inside my spare shoe now. A good pair of sandals can run a surprisingly efficient tournament.

mbm-1272.clue: I sewed the seam in bright green.
mbm-1272.quote: I repaired my friend’s black jacket with the only thread I had. He liked the green line and asked me to carry it down the other sleeve. Our accidental lightning bolt has become his favorite part.

mbm-1273.clue: I roll the rough one last.
mbm-1273.quote: Our bocce set has one old ball with a patch worn smooth on just one side. My uncle calls it unpredictable. I’ve played it so often I can usually guess which way its mood will take it.

mbm-1274.clue: I carry an empty jam jar on hikes.
mbm-1274.quote: At the lookout I lay the lid on my notebook and draw around it. Everything I can see inside that little circle becomes the day’s sketch. My latest jar holds two trees and half a mountain.

mbm-1275.clue: I follow the scent of wild mint.
mbm-1275.quote: My walking trail splits at a damp patch where mint grows by a stone gate. I crush one leaf between my palms there. Even a long muddy walk ends with my hands smelling like the gate.
